scope: IPv4 dhcp-fqdn, dhcp-ignore-clid and dhcp-ttl. TTL parser differences remain open until exact-image evidence and a product fix. Does not qualify unrelated DNS cache or reverse options.

checklist.boundary: Boolean syntax, duplicate flags, unexpected argument; missing default domain and conditional-domain-only configurations reject while literal default with conditional overrides starts.
Live DHCP publication selects address-specific domain; default mode publishes short and qualified names, fqdn-only suppresses only short names. Query A/PTR through UDP and TCP after real ACK.

Name collisions compare case-insensitive short names in default mode and case-insensitive FQDN in fqdn-only mode: different domains coexist only in fqdn-only mode; same-domain collision removes old ownership.
Restore calculates FQDNs after loading all lease short names: same short names in separate domains and duplicate same-domain FQDNs retain C order and publication; restart reproduces it.
Configured authoritative hostname cannot be taken by a client-supplied name; configured names still publish while absent client names do not invent a name.
Hostname option12 and encoded/unencoded option81 feed the same publication mode; domain stripping and case handling use actual C packet responses.
Rename, release and SIGHUP replace only current DHCP names; former forward/PTR ownership disappears and non-DHCP local records remain responsive.
Full DHCP reply, persisted lease identity/name, exact DNS questions/flags/answer values/order/TTL and process/interface cleanup are retained and compared.
Boolean syntax, duplicate flag, unexpected argument and option absent/present baseline.
Same MAC with changing nonempty option61 creates or reuses identity according to the global flag; missing and zero-length IDs follow hardware fallback.
Same nonempty option61 with different MACs moves an existing lease when enabled by default, but distinct hardware identities remain separate when ignored.
Restored nonempty client ID is reused after hardware lookup even with global ignore enabled; verify retained file ID, identity matching and id-based static host selection.
Restart preserves selected identity and release/decline cannot remove an unrelated hardware lease when incoming IDs are ignored.
Full wire reply, allocation address, hostname/client-ID lease rows, DNS health, restart and cleanup compare strictly.
Scalar grammar: absent, explicit empty/zero, positive, INT_MAX, nonnumeric/negative, duplicate directive; inspect exact parser diagnostics and image-libc integer boundaries.
DHCP TTL overrides local-ttl for both qualified/short forward A and PTR while static host TTL retains local-ttl.

Finite lease clamps to exact remaining seconds when configured TTL is larger; scheduled requests occur wholly inside a preselected wall-clock second and wire TTL compares exactly without range normalization.
Infinite lease retains configured TTL including INT_MAX; finite lease with small configured TTL remains fixed across an elapsed second.
Runtime restore and new ACK publication use identical TTL policy across UDP/TCP; zero is an explicit override rather than fallback.
All accepted/rejected startup and --test output, raw clocks/packets, DNS TTLs and cleanup are retained; integer overflow differences are classified explicitly.

resolved_source_findings.policy: explicit wrapping u32 reproduces image musl atoi without Rust overflow; finite ceiling first narrows configured TTL to signed i32, as image rfc1035.c does
